main_text.p: Macedoniâ in Græciam misit,quâ Aratus vinctus in Macedoniam vehéretur. Sed indignissimum fuit,quod tum temporis ab Athenienfibus est commissum.

Nam Macedonum gratiam captantes pro levitate ingenii sui, perlatâ in urbem famâ de Arati interitu, coronas sumpserunt, quod non nisi in magnâ lætitiâ fieri moris erat. Quo audito in iram commotus Aratus sine morâ cum copiis, quas paratas habebat, in Atticam contendit, & obvia vastans ad Academiam usque pervasit: sed confiliis suorum cedens, & precibus sapientissimum civitum victus sine maleficio ulteriore pedem retulit. Quam virtutem populus admiratus, ob eamque in venerationem ejus versus, extincto paulo post Demetrio rege, cum sub pupillo Philippo & tutore ejus Antigono Dosonte res Macedonicæ vacillare viderentur, in spem recuperandæ libertatis erectus Aratum evocavit. Hic quan-quàm ex morbo infirmus tum esset, & præturam non gereret, tamen studio asserendæ in libertatem Græciæ, abjecta memoria contumeliæ prioris lenitica vetus Athenas properavit, annixusque Diogeni Macedonici præsidii præfecto, ut acceptis cL talentis, Pirræum, Munychiam, Salaminem, Sunium,

page.notes: Greek fragment at the bottom left, outside the text block, could not be read and is not transcribed. Two faint ink marks at the left margin near "fuorum" and "Pi-" are not printed text. "cL talentis" is read as printed (150 talents). "vetus" in "lenitica vetus" is a doubtful reading. "Athenas" is read as printed. "sapientissimum" is a doubtful reading: the line shows "sapientio-rum", so the printed word is most likely "sapientiorum"; check against the scan.
